text: Voltaire's Philosophical Dictionary was burned in Geneva, Holland and Berne in 1764 and condemned in Paris in 1765. In 1764 Geneva's city council, prompted by its procurer general, seized and burned copies as an outrage to religion and contrary to Church dogma; only a handful of copies could be found. The book was also burned in Holland and in Berne that year. On 19 March 1765 the Parlement de Paris condemned it to be burned, denouncing its impieties and blasphemies and its attacks on Scripture and theology. Rome placed it on the Index.
